newsitem.title: USA: Hilton seeks to halt ITT break-up in legal filing.
newsitem.headline: Hilton seeks to halt ITT break-up in legal filing.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp. Tuesday filed legal motions in federal court seeking to halt ITT Corp.'s planned breakup into three separate companies, a Hilton spokesman said.

The filing, made in U.S. District Court in Nevada, is Hilton's latest move in its 6-month, $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid for ITT, the New York-based owner of the Sheraton brand hotels and Caesars casinos.

In July, ITT unveiled a comprehensive plan to thwart Hilton's efforts. It intends to split its operations, buy back stock and refinance debt. ITT also filed a motion in federal court seeking a declaratory judgment against Hilton.

Beverly Hills-based Hilton answered ITT's motion in Tuesday's filing. Hilton is seeking a ruling "enjoining the defendants (ITT) from taking any steps to implement the plan," Marc Grossman, senior vice president of corporate affairs, told Reuters.

The suit also asks the court to declare ITT's board has interfered with ITT's shareholders ability to exercise their right of corporate franchise, and it calls on the court to require an ITT shareholder vote on the proposal.
Grossman said the legal filing asks the court for other measures, including rescissions of recent agreements by ITT to sell some of its hotels.
"The plan continues to demonstrate their intent to further entrench management, and it is not at all developed with an eye toward creating value for shareholders," Grossman said.
An ITT spokesman declined to comment on Hilton's filing.

Under its breakup plan, ITT will form three separate companies. One, ITT Destinations, will own the hotels and casinos. The other two will operate ITT's current business for telephone directories and educational services, respectively. It also includes a proposed tender offer for a large block of ITT shares at a price of $70 per share.

ITT's plan does not require shareholder approval and when implemented, will stagger the terms for the board of directors, which financial analysts have cited as a key weakness in ITT's current corporate structure.
Hilton's current bid, which was extended last Friday, is a for $55 a share in cash and stock.
